capabilities.acu_shape: resource-pressure plus ps --sort cpu|memory --max N --max-visited N
capabilities.next: run the unchanged public qjswasm court on Linux and Windows native hosts; do not infer a shared pressure level from free bytes
capabilities.note: The native pressure provider and process ranking are deliberately separate. macOS reports the raw vm.memory_pressure value while CPU and IO are explicitly unavailable; Linux preserves PSI some/full windows for memory, CPU and IO; Windows preserves low/high memory-resource notification booleans while CPU and IO are explicitly unavailable. derived is always false. The existing bounded ps sampler owns CPU and RSS ranking, including scan completeness and detail-error disclosure. The macOS public court is green; Linux and Windows remain pending until their native courts execute the same script.

capabilities.mcu_shape: resource volumes [--max N] with bounded mounted-filesystem capacity facts
capabilities.acu_shape: storage-volumes [--max N] provides bounded mounted-filesystem capacity without physical-device identity
capabilities.next: run the unchanged mounted-volume court on native Linux and Windows; do not restore withdrawn device identity or silently clamp the legacy result ceiling
capabilities.note: The separate storage-volumes facade reports mounted filesystem total, free and current-user-available capacity as exact decimal strings. It keeps current-user available distinct from filesystem free, parses Linux mountinfo as escaped bytes, bounds rows and errors, and never emits backing-device, serial or UUID identifiers. Legacy resource volumes maps to this provider with the archived default 500 made explicit; values above the native 512-row ceiling fail locally rather than being clamped. The native reply deliberately withdraws filesystem device names and derived used percentages. Linux refuses to stat potentially automounting or blocking remote/FUSE filesystems and reports the skipped count. Windows probes only fixed drive-letter and RAM-disk capacity, skips removable/remote media to prevent native error UI or unbounded waits, and marks drive-letter-only coverage incomplete. The public macOS court is green; Linux and Windows have compile evidence but remain pending until native execution.

capabilities.mcu_shape: resource disk [PATH] with exact path-bound filesystem capacity facts
capabilities.acu_shape: storage-volume-at PATH canonicalizes one exact path and reports its kernel-proved mount and complete capacity tuple without device identity
capabilities.next: run the unchanged exact-path volume court on native Linux and Windows; preserve null-plus-reason when Linux mountinfo cannot prove a matching st_dev
capabilities.note: The Bun-free compatibility entry maps resource disk [PATH] to storage-volume-at, with the archived default root path explicit. Files, directories and other existing filesystem entries are canonicalized and symbolic links are followed. Capacity comes from the exact native path query. macOS proves mount identity with statfs f_mntonname; Linux requires both st_dev equality and a component-boundary mountinfo prefix in the current namespace and returns null plus a reason rather than guessing; Windows uses GetVolumePathNameW and labels whether the resolved drive kind belongs to the bounded fixed/RAM inventory. Replies expose canonical and mount paths but never device/source names, fsids, volume GUIDs or serials. The public macOS court proves directory/file parity and mounted-inventory identity; Linux and Windows remain pending native execution.
